answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the island index resolves every citation against the hollow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the karst audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 188 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 188 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 40 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
